kind: Original conditional analytical extension; potential acceleration, not replicated performance
source_scope: Schwabe2016 Chapter2pp19-20 andChapter5pp77-78 known item difficulties with Rasch responses; original sumscore comparator instead rescales totals and uses Gaussian phenotype model.
assumptions: Known fixed finite item difficulties b_j
Conditionally independent Bernoulli responses with logit p_j=theta-b_j
All retained observed items and their difficulties/missingness pattern known
Parameters being inferred occur only through latent theta law; item calibration not estimated
proof: For a response vector y with S=sum(y_j), p(y|theta,b)=exp(S*theta-sum(b_j*y_j))/product_j(1+exp(theta-b_j)).
Let c_s(b) be the coefficient of z^s in product_j(1+exp(-b_j)*z). Summing patterns at fixed S=s gives p(S=s|theta,b)=c_s(b)*exp(s*theta)/product_j(1+exp(theta-b_j)).

Their ratio exp(-sum(b_j*y_j))/c_S(b) is constant in theta and every latent-model parameter. For multiple people, multiply these constants, integrate the same correlated latent law and multiply the same priors. The normalized posterior on all latent-model quantities is identical.

Thus exact score-likelihood calculation can preserve the item model, even for non-Gaussian moderated ACE latent laws. This does not justify the dissertation Gaussian/rescaled sumscore comparator and says nothing about its bias.

If item parameters are inferred, the dropped constants depend on them, so retaining only S generally loses calibration information. With different observed-item masks the corresponding b subset and mask must be retained; missingness ignorability is a separate assumption.
possible_next_engine_work: A custom exact score likelihood could reduce graph size, but denominator stilldepends on every difficulty. No benchmark or implementation here. Need stable coefficient/loglikelihood implementation and independent target/procedure validation before sampling.
